document.title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's sparse storage causes external_prefix_cache_hits_total to be permanently 0
document.body:
## Summary

When serving **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark** (`--speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", ...}'`) with the native `OffloadingConnector` (`--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector",...}'`), the external (RAM-tier) prefix cache **never records a hit**, even under sustained real load with GPU eviction happening (`kv_cache_usage` >95%, `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total` growing steadily into the hundreds of GB). `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stays at exactly `0` for the lifetime of the server, while `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries_total` grows into the millions.

Root cause: DSpark adds 3 extra decoder layers purely for speculative drafting (`DSparkDeepseekV4Model`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`). vLLM correctly classifies this layer group's `GroupOffloadConfig.is_eagle_group = True`. `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._lookup()` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`) requires **every** KV-cache group to independently report a nonzero hit; any single group reporting `num_hit_blocks == 0` immediately short-circuits the **entire request's** lookup to `0` (`if num_hit_blocks == 0: return 0`, inside the per-group loop).

The DSpark group's own store IS occurring (verified via `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total`), but its stored blocks are **sparse and discontinuous**: added per-key debug instrumentation confirmed real `HIT` results scattered among mostly `MISS` results (e.g. `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]` scanning newest-first), never forming the consecutive run `_sliding_window_lookup` requires (`sliding_window_size_in_blocks + 1` for eagle groups, to account for the "trailing volatile block" compensation). Because this specific group can essentially never satisfy the consecutive-hit requirement for DSpark's block-based drafting pattern, it permanently poisons the AND-combination for the whole request: even though the model's *real* KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently measured a working 88.9%–100% hit rate once isolated from this effect.

## Related issues (different code path, same root pattern)

This looks superficially similar to a well-known family of bugs where an eagle/draft
KV-cache group breaks multi-group cache-hit coordination, but all of those live in the
**GPU-side** `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`/`find_longest_cache_hit()` radix-cache path
(`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`), not in the **CPU-offload** `OffloadingConnector`
path this issue is about:

- #32802: GPT-OSS 0% prefix cache hits with hybrid attention + EAGLE (the original
  "EAGLE spiral block-dropping" report; GPU hybrid coordinator).
- #33524: partial fix for #32802 via an `is_simple_hybrid` guard (`len(attention_groups) == 2`).
- #40624: Gemma4 + DFlash hits the same spiral because it has 3 groups, not 2, so the
  `is_simple_hybrid` guard from #33524 doesn't cover it.
- #42948: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (no speculative decoding) loses first-block GPU cache
  entries on reassignment; same "eagle/multi-group intersection" family, again GPU-side.

I confirmed (by reading `kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py` directly and by
reproducing on this exact model/config) that this issue's bug is **not** the same code
path as any of the above: `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._lookup()` has its own,
separate AND-combination logic for the CPU/RAM tier, with no interaction with
`HybridKVCacheCoordinator`. I could not find an existing issue covering this specific
code path, hence filing separately, but flagging the connection since whoever
reviews this may recognize the general pattern from the issues above.

## Repro

- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` (43 hidden layers + 3 DSpark draft layers + 1 MTP layer), `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--block-size 256`, `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.
- `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":<N>}}'`
- `--speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "draft_sample_method": "greedy"}'`
- vLLM: nightly build `cu129-nightly-09663abde0f50944a8d5ea30120666024b503faa` (`0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde`)
- Workload: real multi-turn conversational replay (SWE-agent-style sessions), concurrency=64, sustained load causing genuine GPU KV eviction (`kv_cache_usage_max` ~99%).
- Observed: `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` = `0` for the entire run; `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries_total` in the millions; `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total` in the hundreds of GB.

## Diagnostic evidence

Added temporary debug logging to `_lookup()` printing per-group `group_idx`, `sliding_window_blocks`, `offloaded_block_size`, `num_hit_blocks`, and `is_eagle_group`. Sample from a live run:

```
group_idx=0 sliding_window_blocks=None offloaded_block_size=256 is_eagle=False: 279/2514 miss  (88.9% hit)
group_idx=1 sliding_window_blocks=2    offloaded_block_size=64  is_eagle=False: 0/2235 miss    (100% hit)
group_idx=2 sliding_window_blocks=2    offloaded_block_size=64  is_eagle=True:  66/66 miss     (0% hit, always)
group_idx=4 sliding_window_blocks=16   offloaded_block_size=8   is_eagle=False: 0/2235 miss    (100% hit)
```

Per-key trace for group_idx=2 (the DSpark draft group), confirming data exists but is non-consecutive:

```
required_window=3 per_key(newest-first)=[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]  RESULT=0
required_window=3 per_key(newest-first)=[MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]        RESULT=0
```

## Suggested fix

**Scoping note**: `is_eagle_group` is a generic vLLM flag set for *any* model using
an EAGLE-family draft attention group (standard EAGLE/EAGLE3, MTP, DFlash, DSpark,
...), not something DSpark-specific. The existing `TestEagle` suite in
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` shows the
current "pop one volatile trailing block" mechanism (query one extra block,
subtract 1 from the hit count once verified) works correctly and provides real
cross-request reuse for well-behaved EAGLE/MTP/DFlash models: it's not itself
broken. DSpark's draft-layer KV is architecturally different: it's recomputed from
the target model's real hidden state every step
(`DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv`), so its stored content has
*no* reuse value at all, not merely "one volatile tail block": that's why its
lookup is sparse/discontinuous throughout rather than just failing at the boundary.

Patch (`_lookup()` in `OffloadingConnectorScheduler`): when a group flagged
`is_eagle_group` reports `num_hit_blocks == 0`, drop *that one group* from the rest
of the current lookup call instead of returning 0 for the whole request, but only
when `speculative_config.use_dspark()` is true (`SchedulerOffloadConfig.is_dspark`,
computed once from `spec.vllm_config.speculative_config.use_dspark()`). The excluded
set is tracked on the request's state (`RequestOffloadState.lookup_excluded_groups`)
so `update_state_after_alloc` skips `prepare_load` for those specific groups (to
avoid `assert block is not None` in `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load`, since their
keys were never confirmed present for the boundary the surviving groups settled
on). `_build_store_jobs` is untouched entirely: storage keeps the existing "pop one
trailing block" behavior for every eagle-family method, including DSpark.

- For EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, and DFlash: `is_dspark` is always False, so the new branch
  is **unreachable**: `_lookup()` takes the exact original `return 0` path,
  byte-for-byte identical to before this change.
- For DSpark: a 0-hit draft group is excluded from the current lookup call instead
  of zeroing out co-existing non-eagle groups' real, reusable hits.
- Small diff: only `_lookup()`, `update_state_after_alloc()`, and one new field each
  on `SchedulerOffloadConfig` (`is_dspark`) and `RequestOffloadState`
  (`lookup_excluded_groups`). `__init__`'s group classification and
  `_build_store_jobs` are untouched.

**Verification**:
- Unit tests: added 3 tests to `TestEagle` (`test_sparse_eagle_group_does_not_poison_other_groups_lookup`, `test_non_dspark_eagle_group_miss_still_zeros_whole_request`, `test_sparse_eagle_group_load_excludes_only_the_failing_group`), covering the DSpark-sparse-storage lookup/load path and explicitly proving the branch is unreachable when `is_dspark=False`. Ran the full `TestEagle` class (21 tests: 18 pre-existing + 3 new) against this exact vLLM build: all pass, confirming no regression to the existing EAGLE/MTP/DFlash "pop one trailing block" tests.
- Production validation: 600s sustained load, concurrency=64, real multi-turn conversational replay, 100% request success rate (0 failures), zero crashes. `external_prefix_cache_hits_total`/`queries_total` recovered to **~83.7%** combined hit rate (up from a permanent 0%), consistent with the GPU-side prefix cache hit rate (83.3%) measured in the same run.
- Correctness: the "same prompt, different completion" variance I initially suspected as a correctness bug turned out to be a pre-existing property of DSpark speculative decoding under concurrent batched serving (reproduced identically on a baseline server with *no* KV-transfer connector at all, i.e. unrelated to this change).

I initially prototyped a simpler, blanket "exclude every `is_eagle_group` group
unconditionally" version (no `is_dspark` check, touching `__init__` and
`_build_store_jobs` too) and load-tested it successfully as well, but did not pursue
it further once I realized it would silently disable the *working* "pop one
trailing block" reuse for every other eagle-family method, not just DSpark: the
`is_dspark`-gated version above is what I'd like feedback on / propose as the actual
fix.

Happy to open a PR with this change (patch + the 3 regression tests) if the
approach looks right: flagging as an issue first since this touches shared logic
used by every eagle-family speculative-decoding + KV-offloading combination, not
just DSpark, and I'd like a scope sanity-check before submitting.

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde` (image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu129-nightly-09663abde0f50944a8d5ea30120666024b503faa`)
- GPUs: 4x (TP=4)
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`
